offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: False alarm. The ledger consumer group is not 250 messages behind. Its lag on provider-events stayed at 0 to 1 from 19:49 through 19:54, when the alert fired. The ledger posts events about as fast as payment-confirmer confirms them. The money check settled in 0.24s and all five invariants passed, so every provider event up to the cutoff was booked exactly once. The stack came up at 19:48:52 and nothing has restarted or changed since. The 250 figure most likely comes from the alert rule: a bad expression or labels (the metric has consumer, partition, service_instance_id, service_name, not consumer_group), a stale series from before bring-up, or an injected test alert. I could not see the rule, so its exact fault stays open. A spike shorter than my 60s samples is possible but would have cleared almost at once, and nothing was lost.

evidence.shows: Ledger consumer lag summed by consumer is 0 to 1 from 19:49 to 19:54:26, never near 250. payment-confirmer is at 0.

All containers are running and healthy with 0 restarts. ledger-consumer started at 19:49:00.
The only deploys are the initial bring-up at 19:48:52. Ledger settings are normal (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter). No later change could cause a backlog.
